subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Inductors: Magnetism Meets Electricity
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Inductors: Magnetism Meets Electricity.

hook.text: An inductor resists changes in current. Try to increase the flow and it pushes back magnetically.

buildup.text: A wire coil creates a magnetic field when current flows. Changing the current changes the field, inducing opposing voltage.

discovery.text: Inductance is measured in henrys. It depends on the number of coil turns, core material, and coil dimensions.

twist.text: Transformers are two inductors sharing a magnetic core. Energy transfers between them without any electrical connection.

climax.text: Wireless phone chargers use induction. A coil in the pad creates a field that a coil in the phone captures.

punchline.text: Coil some wire. Run current through it. Magnetism does the rest.

quiz.question: How do wireless phone chargers transfer energy?
options: Microwaves carry energy from the pad to the phone's antenna
A coil in the pad creates a magnetic field that a coil in the phone captures via induction
Tiny electrical contacts in the pad connect to the phone case
